name: Louvre Museum
cardImageAlt: The glass pyramid entrance of the Louvre Museum in Paris
cardTagline: Home to the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo, and 35,000+ works of art.
heroSubheading: Book official skip-the-line tickets and guided tours for the world's most visited museum. See the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo, and centuries of art under I. M. Pei's glass pyramid.
heroImageAlt: The Louvre Museum glass pyramid illuminated at dusk
highlightsSubheading: The Louvre holds over 35,000 works across eight departments spanning 9,000 years of history. These are the pieces most visitors come to see first.

highlights.title: The Mona Lisa
highlights.body: Leonardo da Vinci's iconic portrait, displayed behind protective glass in the Salle des États — the museum's single most-visited work.

highlights.title: Venus de Milo
highlights.body: The armless marble goddess of ancient Greece, one of the most celebrated sculptures ever recovered.

highlights.title: Winged Victory of Samothrace
highlights.body: A dramatic Hellenistic sculpture perched at the top of the Daru staircase, celebrating a naval triumph.

highlights.title: The Glass Pyramid
highlights.body: I. M. Pei's 1989 glass-and-steel pyramid over the Cour Napoléon, now as iconic as the palace itself.

aboutBody:
Originally a 12th-century fortress and later a royal palace, the Louvre became a public museum in 1793. Today it is the world's largest and most-visited art museum, housing masterpieces from ancient civilizations through the mid-19th century across the Sully, Denon, and Richelieu wings.

Because of the museum's sheer size, most first-time visitors plan a route in advance — trying to see everything in one visit is not realistic. A skip-the-line ticket or guided tour is the easiest way to make sure your time inside is spent looking at art rather than waiting outside the pyramid.
toursSubheading: Timed-entry tickets and guided tours, including options that pair the Louvre with other top Paris sights.
practicalHoursNote: Last entry is 60 minutes before closing. Hours can change for holidays — always check your ticket's confirmed time slot.
practicalAddress:
Rue de Rivoli, 75001 Paris, France.
Main entrance via the glass pyramid in the Cour Napoléon; a second entrance is available via the Carrousel du Louvre at 99 Rue de Rivoli.
practicalGettingThere: Métro: Palais-Royal–Musée du Louvre (Lines 1 & 7), directly beneath the museum.
practicalBestTimeBody: Wednesday and Friday evenings (open until 9:45 PM) are noticeably quieter than daytime hours. If you can only visit during the day, arrive right at opening time to beat the tour-group rush to the Mona Lisa.
priceSubheading: Find the right ticket for your visit — from standard timed entry to small-group guided tours.
priceNote: Since January 2026 the Louvre uses two-tier pricing: a lower rate for EEA residents and a standard rate for non-EEA visitors. Under-18s and EU/EEA residents aged 18–25 enter free with valid ID (booking fee may still apply on third-party tickets).

name: Duomo Florence
cardImageAlt: Florence Cathedral Santa Maria del Fiore and Brunelleschi's Dome
cardTagline: Climb Brunelleschi's Dome and explore Florence's Renaissance cathedral complex.
heroSubheading: Official Duomo tickets with guaranteed Dome Climb access. Skip the line and experience the history, art and breathtaking views of Florence Cathedral.
heroImageAlt: Florence Cathedral Brunelleschi Dome and skyline
highlightsEyebrow: The Heart of the Italian Renaissance
highlightsHeading: 5 Must-See Wonders of the Florence Duomo Complex
highlightsSubheading: Commissioned in 1296 and capped by Filippo Brunelleschi's architectural marvel in 1436, the Piazza del Duomo complex is one of Italy's greatest Renaissance treasures.

highlights.title: Brunelleschi's Dome Climb (463 Steps)
highlights.body: Ascend between the double masonry shells of the world's largest brick dome and step onto the lantern terrace for 360° views across Florence.

highlights.title: Vasari's Last Judgment Frescoes
highlights.body: Gaze up at 3,600 square meters of Renaissance frescoes painted by Giorgio Vasari and Federico Zuccari.

highlights.title: Giotto's Bell Tower
highlights.body: Climb 414 steps up Giotto's 85-meter free-standing bell tower for the iconic close-up view of Brunelleschi's dome.

highlights.title: Baptistery & Gates of Paradise
highlights.body: Marvel at Ghiberti's gilded bronze doors and the 13th-century golden Byzantine ceiling mosaics inside the octagonal Baptistery.

aboutBody:
The Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore is the heart of Florence. Climb the dome designed by Filippo Brunelleschi, explore centuries of art and history across the wider cathedral complex, and enjoy unforgettable views over the city and the Tuscan hills beyond.

Because Dome Climb time slots are strictly limited for safety reasons, they sell out weeks in advance during peak season — booking ahead is essential if climbing the dome is on your list.
toursSubheading: Inclusive passes, fast-track priority tickets, and expert-led Renaissance tours.
practicalHoursNote: Entry to the main cathedral nave is free, but queues can exceed 2 hours. Access to the Dome, Tower, Baptistery, Museum, and Crypt requires an official pass.
practicalAddress:
Piazza del Duomo, 50122 Firenze (FI), Italy.
Located in the pedestrian heart of historic Florence.
practicalGettingThere: 10-minute walk from Firenze Santa Maria Novella (SMN) railway station.
practicalBestTimeHeading: Best Time to Climb the Dome
practicalBestTimeBody: The 8:15 AM or 9:00 AM morning slots offer the coolest temperatures and calmest light before crowds peak. The 5:30 PM – 6:30 PM evening slots provide golden-hour light over the Florentine rooftops.

priceNote: All passes include digital barcode access valid for 3 days from first entry. Free cancellation up to 24 hours prior on verified tickets.

name: Uffizi Gallery
cardImageAlt: The Uffizi Gallery courtyard in Florence
cardTagline: Botticelli's Birth of Venus, Renaissance masterworks, and Florence's finest art collection.
heroSubheading: Book skip-the-line Uffizi Gallery tickets and guided tours to see Botticelli's Birth of Venus, works by Michelangelo, Raphael, and Leonardo, in one of the world's greatest Renaissance art collections.
heroImageAlt: Uffizi Gallery corridor lined with classical sculpture in Florence
highlightsSubheading: Housed in a 16th-century palazzo just steps from the Duomo, the Uffizi holds one of the finest collections of Italian Renaissance painting anywhere in the world.

highlights.title: Birth of Venus
highlights.body: Sandro Botticelli's masterpiece, one of the most reproduced paintings of the Italian Renaissance.

highlights.title: Primavera
highlights.body: Another Botticelli icon, packed with mythological figures and allegory, hung nearby the Birth of Venus.

highlights.title: Renaissance Masters
highlights.body: Works by Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael, and Titian across galleries overlooking the Arno and Piazza della Signoria.

highlights.title: The Vasari Corridor Views
highlights.body: Long palazzo galleries with sweeping views over central Florence, connecting the Uffizi to the Palazzo Vecchio.

aboutBody:
Originally built in 1560 as offices ('uffizi') for the Florentine magistrates under Cosimo I de' Medici, the building was converted into a gallery for the Medici family's art collection and opened to the public in 1765 — making it one of the oldest museums in the world.

Because the Uffizi is one of Florence's most in-demand museums, timed-entry tickets regularly sell out days in advance in high season. Booking ahead — ideally paired with your Duomo visit given the short walk between the two — is the easiest way to guarantee entry.
toursSubheading: Timed-entry tickets, afternoon discount slots, and guided tours led by local art historians.
practicalHoursNote: An afternoon discount rate applies to entry from 4:00 PM onward. First Sunday of the month is free, but tickets cannot be booked online for it and queues are long.
practicalAddress:
Piazzale degli Uffizi, 50122 Firenze (FI), Italy.
Between Palazzo Vecchio and the Arno river, a short walk from the Duomo.
practicalGettingThere: 5-minute walk from Piazza del Duomo; 15-minute walk from Firenze Santa Maria Novella station.
practicalBestTimeBody: Book the 4:00 PM afternoon-discount slot for a quieter visit at a lower price, or arrive right at 8:15 AM opening to beat the day's tour groups.
priceSubheading: Standard timed entry, afternoon discount tickets, and small-group guided tours compared side by side.
priceNote: Under-18s enter free year-round with valid ID. Prices and time slots are subject to the Uffizi's own seasonal rules.

name: Lindt Home of Chocolate
cardImageAlt: The Lindt Home of Chocolate building in Kilchberg, Switzerland
cardTagline: The world's largest Lindt chocolate fountain and an interactive journey through chocolate-making.
heroHeading: Lindt Home of Chocolate Tickets & Tour
heroSubheading: Book tickets to the Lindt Home of Chocolate near Zurich — home to the world's tallest chocolate fountain, an interactive multimedia exhibition, and a chocolate shop with treats made on site.
heroImageAlt: The world's largest chocolate fountain inside the Lindt Home of Chocolate
highlightsHeading: Must-See Highlights at the Lindt Home of Chocolate
highlightsSubheading: Opened in 2020 in a striking building by architects Christ & Gantenbein, the museum guides visitors through seven interactive "chocolate worlds."

highlights.title: The Giant Chocolate Fountain
highlights.body: A nine-meter chocolate fountain — the tallest of its kind in the world — cascading with real Lindt chocolate.

highlights.title: Cocoa Bean to Bar Journey
highlights.body: An interactive multimedia exhibition tracing chocolate's origins in Central America through to the modern Lindt factory.

highlights.title: Chocolateria Live Demonstrations
highlights.body: Watch chocolatiers hand-make pralines and treats in a working show kitchen.

highlights.title: The World's Largest Lindt Shop
highlights.body: A flagship Lindt boutique stocked with exclusive pralines and treats not sold elsewhere.

aboutHeading: About the Lindt Home of Chocolate
aboutBody:
The Lindt Home of Chocolate sits on the shore of Lake Zurich in Kilchberg, next to the original Lindt & Sprüngli factory where the company has produced chocolate since 1899. The museum opened to the public in 2020 as a modern, interactive complement to the historic factory.

Because the museum is popular with families and school groups, booking a timed ticket in advance is recommended, especially on weekends and during Swiss school holidays.
toursHeading: Choose Your Lindt Home of Chocolate Ticket
toursSubheading: Standard museum entry and combined ticket options for visiting Kilchberg from Zurich.
practicalHoursNote: Open 360 days a year. Booking online in advance is recommended due to high demand, especially on weekends.
practicalAddress:
Schokoladenplatz 1, 8802 Kilchberg, Switzerland.
On the shore of Lake Zurich, next to the Lindt & Sprüngli factory.
practicalGettingThere: S-Bahn (S8) from Zurich Hauptbahnhof to Kilchberg station, then a short signposted walk; also reachable by Lake Zurich boat in summer.
practicalBestTimeBody: Weekday mornings are quietest. Weekends and Swiss school holidays draw the largest crowds, particularly around the chocolate fountain and tasting stations.

priceSubheading: Individual and family tickets for the museum, with seasonal discounts where available.
priceNote: Prices are shown in Swiss Francs (CHF). Group rates are available separately for parties of 20 or more via the official Lindt Home of Chocolate website.
